translations.text: Paul and Timothy, servants of Jesus Christ, to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are in Philippi, to the bishops and deacons:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I give thanks to my God at every remembrance of you;
always, in all my prayers for all of you, I make prayer with joy
because of your fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now,
with hope in this very thing, that he who began a good work among you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ.

Just as it is right for me to think this about all of you, because I remember you in my heart, in my bonds and in the defense and confirmation of the gospel, so that all of you may be sharers with me in the grace.
God is my witness how I long for you with the compassion of Christ Jesus;
and I also pray this, that your love may overflow more and more with knowledge and all discernment,
so that you may test what is better and be true and without stumbling until the day of Christ Jesus,
filled with the fruit of righteousness through Christ Jesus, for the glory and praise of God.
I want you to know, brothers, that what has happened to me has come about rather for the advancement of the gospel,
so that these bonds of mine have become known in Christ throughout the whole palace and to all others,
and that most of the brothers in the Lord, trusting because of my bonds, all the more dare [? the text reads 'I dare'] to speak the word of God without fear.
Some preach Christ out of envy and strife, others out of goodwill;
some out of love: they know that I stand for the defense of the gospel.
Others proclaim Christ out of strife, impurely, thinking to bring afflictions upon these bonds of mine.
What then? Yet in every way, whether by pretext or in truth, Christ is preached, and for this I rejoice and will rejoice.
I know that this will result in salvation for me through your supplication and the help of the Spirit of Christ Jesus,
according to my expectation and hope that I shall be ashamed in nothing, but that with all boldness, as always, so now also Christ will be glorified in my body, whether by life or by death.
For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
If life in this flesh is the fruit of my work, then which I should choose I do not know.
I am held fast between these two: my heart tells me to depart and be with Christ, which is much better.
But to remain in the flesh is rather [?] for your sake.
And in this hope I know that I shall remain and [?] with all of you for the advancement and joy of the faith,
So that your boasting may abound in Christ Jesus because of me, through my coming to you again.

Only let us walk worthily of the gospel of Christ, so that whether I come and see you, or am far away and hear about you, that you stand firm in one spirit and one mind, you may be fellow-strivers in the faith of the gospel,
and do not be frightened in anything by those who oppose you, which is for them a sign of destruction, but for you, of salvation; and this is from God.
For it has been granted to you for Christ's sake not only to have faith in him, but also to suffer for him.
Have the same struggle that you saw in me and now hear about from me.
Whatever consolation there is from Christ, and whatever consolation of love, whatever communion of the Spirit, whatever compassion and mercy,
make my joy complete, so that you think the same thing and have the same love; be of one soul and one mind,
doing nothing out of rivalry or vain conceit, but in humility let each of you regard the other as greater than himself.
Let each one of you not [?] seek only what is his own, but each of you also what is his neighbor's.
Let this mind be considered among you, which was also from Christ Jesus.
Who, being the image of God, did not regard it as plunder for himself to be equal to God,
but he diminished himself and took on the form of a slave, and became like human beings, and in form became as a man;
he humbled himself and became obedient unto death, even death on the cross.
Therefore God also exalted him exceedingly and bestowed on him the name that is above all names,
so that at the name of Jesus Christ every knee should bend, of those in heaven and on earth and under the earth,
and every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
And now, my beloved, just as you have always been obedient, not only at my coming but now much more in my being far away, work for your salvation with fear and trembling.
For it is God who works in you both the will and the help for the sake of good pleasure.
Do everything without grumbling and inner disputing,
so that you may be spotless and innocent, children of God, undefiled in the midst of a crooked and perverse generation, so that you may shine like luminaries in the world.
Hold the word of life, as a boast for me on the day of Christ, that I am not running in vain, nor have I toiled in vain.
Even if I am offered up upon this sacrifice and service of your faith, I rejoice, and I rejoice with all of you.
In the same way you too rejoice, and rejoice with me.
And I hope in Christ Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, so that I too may be glad of heart when I learn about you.
For I have no one else so faithful, who would care for you from the heart.
For all seek their own interests and not those of Christ Jesus.
But you know his proven character, that as a son with a father, so he served the gospel with me.
This one I hope to send, when I have settled what concerns me, from him [?].
But I trust in the Lord that I too shall come soon.
I have considered it better to send to you Epaphroditus, our brother, my fellow helper and fellow struggler, your messenger and the minister to my needs,
for he was longing for all of you and eager, because you had heard that he had fallen ill.
Truly he fell ill, to the point of death; but God had mercy on him, and not on him only but on me also, so that sorrow should not be added to me upon sorrow.
I have sent him quickly, so that you may see him and rejoice again, and that I may be free of care.
Receive him in the Lord with all joy, and hold such people in honor,
for on account of the work of Christ he came as far as death, offering up his life, so that he might fulfill that service toward me which was lacking on your part.
From now on, brothers, rejoice in the Lord! To write the same things to you is not wearisome for me, and for you it is a safeguard.
Beware of the dogs, beware of the evil workers, watch out for the mutilation,
for we are the circumcision, we who serve by the Spirit of God and boast in Christ Jesus and do not trust in the flesh,
though I do have hope even from the flesh; if anyone thinks he has some other hope in the flesh, I have more:
by circumcision of the eighth day, of the race of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews, by the law a Pharisee,
in zeal I persecuted the churches, in the righteousness of the law I was blameless.
But what was gain to me, this I have counted as loss for the sake of Christ.

Indeed, I also count everything as loss on account of the surpassing knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord, for whose sake I have suffered the loss of everything, and I count it as refuse, so that I may gain Christ
and be found in him, not having my own righteousness from the law, but through faith in Jesus Christ, the righteousness from God by that faith,
to know him and the power of his resurrection and the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformed to his death,
so that I may somehow attain also to the resurrection from the dead.
Not that I have already received it or am already made perfect; but I press on so that I may overtake that for which I also was taken hold of by Christ Jesus.
Brothers, I no longer count myself as having attained; but this one thing I do: I forget what is behind and reach out toward what is ahead,
with care I press on toward the crown of the heavenly calling of God in Christ Jesus.
As many of us as are perfect, let us think this; and if we think anything else, God will reveal that too to you.
However, to whatever point we have attained, let us think the same thing and stand by the same line [?].
Be fellow imitators of me, brothers, and observe those who walk in this way, just as we are a pattern for you.
For many walk about, of whom I have told you many times, and now I tell you with weeping, concerning those enemies of the cross of Christ,
whose end is destruction, whose god is the belly and whose glory is in their shame, who think about the things of the earth.
But our dwelling place is in the heavens, from where we await the Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ,
who will transform these bodies of our lowliness, so that they may be conformed to the body of his glory, according to the working of his power and his subjecting all things to himself.
From now on, my beloved and longed-for brothers, my joys and my crowns, stand firm in this way, beloved.
I beseech Euodia and I beseech Syntyche: think the same thought in the Lord.

Yes, I beseech you too, faithful yoke-fellow: receive those women, who struggled together with me in the gospel, along with Clement, those fellow helpers of mine, and others, whose names are in the book of life.
Rejoice always in the Lord; again I say to you: rejoice.
Let your humility be known to all people. The Lord is near.
Do not be anxious about anything, but with all prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God,
and may the peace of God, which surpasses all minds, make firm your hearts and your minds through Christ Jesus.
From now on, brothers, whatever is true, whatever is good, whatever is righteous, whatever is purity, whatever is lovely, whatever is praiseworthy, virtuous and praised, think about that.
What you learned and received and heard and saw in me, do that also; and may the God of peace be with you.
I rejoiced greatly in the Lord, because now at last you have sprouted anew in thinking on my behalf, which you had indeed been thinking about, and you were also generous [?].
I do not say this to you because of any want, for I have learned to be content in whatever state I am.
I know both being brought low and I know being raised up; in regard to all things and in everything I have been trained: to be full and to hunger, to abound and to lack.
I am able to do all things through him who strengthened me.
Yet you did this well too, in that you shared with me in these afflictions of mine.
And you also know this, Philippians, that at the beginning of the gospel, when I went out from Macedonia, not one church shared with me in the matter of giving and receiving, except you alone.
For even to Thessalonica you sent to me for my need once and twice.
It is not that I seek the gift; rather, I seek the fruit that increases to your credit.
I have everything and have abundance; I am filled, having received from Epaphroditus what came from you, with a breath of fragrance, an offered sacrifice pleasing to God.
And may my God fill your every need according to his riches, in glory through Christ Jesus.
And to our God and Father be glory forever and ever. Amen.
Greet all the saints in Christ Jesus. The brothers who are with me greet you.
All the saints greet you, and especially those of the household of Caesar.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
